and the catalog are the authority for the counts; the parity check compares
them at startup. `render_frame` writes a PNG and returns its path; `export`
puts the job on the Export Queue and answers an `export_id` at once, and
`export_status` answers it until `done` (`mcp.py`'s `export_with` waits; spec
§11 #326).

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

1	# Handoff: documentation site theme (Boppa Llewyn redesign)
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	This handoff moves the documentation site (`docs/site/`) from the old Boppa Llewyn theme to the new Boppa Llewyn design system. The old theme imitated a furniture workshop: Cormorant Garamond display type, IBM Plex, warm-ebony greys, a cream light look, a brass accent and 2/4/8 px "joinery" corners. The new system is the one the company website and every app's docs share:
6	
7	- **Type:** Geist for text, Geist Mono for eyebrows, code, keys and versions. No serif anywhere.
8	- **Colour:** neutral greys, with the logo green as the one accent. The app icons and the company mark supply the rest of the colour.
9	- **Shape:** 6/10/16 px corners. Hairlines separate things; shadows are limited to a 1 px card shadow and the screenshot window.
10	- **Brand:** the company mark (three toy blocks) and the name in the header, with the product after it: **Boppa Llewyn / Frame Job**.
11	
12	Decisions confirmed by the owner:
13	
14	- The new Boppa Llewyn design system replaces the old theme everywhere.
15	- The company mark is the building-blocks mark (`assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg`).
16	- Body type is sans-serif; nothing is set in a serif.
17	
18	Not yet confirmed: which palette ships. This handoff ships **Neutral Light** for the light look and **Neutral Dark** for the dark look, the pair the design system recommends. The system also has three alternates (Cream & Coral, Field Green, Monochrome). They're in `tokens.css` and switchable in the reference page, so the owner can compare. Changing the palette later means changing two blocks of `tokens.css` and nothing else.
19	
20	## About the design files
21	
22	`Docs Theme.html` is a **design reference in HTML**: a static mock of a content page and the splash page, not Starlight's markup. Recreate it in the existing Starlight theme files. Map each part by the tables below, and don't copy the mock's class names. Open it from this folder in a browser (it loads Geist from Google Fonts and the real screens and mark from `docs/site/src/assets/`). The bar at the top switches page, look and palette; `?theme=dark&page=splash&bare=1` does the same from the URL.
23	
24	## Fidelity
25	
26	**High fidelity** for colour, type, spacing, corners and borders, in both looks, at 1440 px and 390 px. The page structure doesn't change: the 280 px sidebar and 680 px prose column are the site's current widths, and the table of contents keeps Starlight's own width (224 px in the mock). The header grows from 60 to 64 px (`--sl-nav-height: 4rem`). Icons in the mock are simple stand-ins; keep Starlight's own icons.
27	
28	## Files
29	
30	| File | What it is |
31	|---|---|
32	| `Docs Theme.html` | **The spec.** Content page (Split clips) and splash, light and dark, desktop and phone. |
33	| `tokens.css` | Every colour, shadow, spacing, radius and font token as `--bl-*` custom properties: Neutral Light under `[data-theme='light']`, Neutral Dark under `[data-theme='dark']`, the three alternate palettes at the end. Generated from the design system; copy it into the site whole rather than retyping values. The type scale is in its closing comment. |
34	| `assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | The company mark, 1024 × 1024 on the cream app-icon plate. |
35	
36	## What changes, file by file
37	
38	All paths are under `docs/site/`.
39	
40	| File | Change |
41	|---|---|
42	| `src/styles/boppa-llewyn.css` | Rewritten on the new tokens: the old `--bl-*` block is replaced by `tokens.css`, the `--sl-*` mapping follows the table below, and every rule below "Site layer" is restyled to the mock. Keep its structure (tokens, mapping, base rules, then the parts Starlight's variables can't reach) and its rule of preferring CSS over overrides. |
43	| `src/styles/frame-job.css` | `Shot`, `AtAGlance` and the feature index restyled (below). |
44	| `src/fonts/font-face.css`, `public/fonts/` | Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex removed; Geist and Geist Mono added (below). |
45	| `astro.config.mjs` | `logo` points at the blocks mark; the two `preload` links name the Geist files; `expressiveCode.styleOverrides` follow "Code blocks". |
46	| `src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | New: copied from this folder. `src/assets/logo.svg` (the Frame Job mark) stays, for the splash hero and anywhere the product is shown. |
47	| `src/components/SiteTitle.astro` | The lockup (below). |
48	| `src/components/Shot.astro` | One new optional prop, `frame`, for full-window captures (below). |
49	| `src/content/docs/index.mdx` | The editor-window `Shot` gains `frame`. No other content changes. |
50	| `README.md` ("Theme") | Rewritten to describe the new system: the families, the palette pair, the files. |
51	| `CLAUDE.md` | The `src/fonts/, public/fonts/` row names the new faces, if it names them. |
52	
53	`ThemeSelect.astro`, `PageTitle.astro` and `Hero.astro` keep their markup; they change through CSS only. `public/favicon.svg` stays the Frame Job icon, because the tab belongs to the product.
54	
55	## Fonts
56	
57	- **Geist** (variable, weights 100 to 900) and **Geist Mono** (variable, 100 to 900), both under the SIL Open Font Licence 1.1. Take the `latin` and `latin-ext` WOFF2 subsets from Google Fonts, as the current faces were. Self-host them in `public/fonts/` as now, split by `unicode-range` in `font-face.css`.
58	- Replace `public/fonts/OFL.txt` with Geist's licence text (it names the Geist Project Authors). Delete every Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex file and rule; nothing uses them afterwards.
59	- Preload the two `latin` files, Geist and Geist Mono: the page's first screen has both (the header's version badge and the page eyebrow are mono).
60	- `--sl-font: var(--bl-font-sans)` and `--sl-font-mono: var(--bl-font-mono)`. The stacks in `tokens.css` fall back to the Mac's own San Francisco and SF Mono. Remove `--bl-font-display` and every rule that sets headings in it.
61	
62	## Starlight's colour variables
63	
64	Map these in both looks; each value is a token from `tokens.css`, so the light and dark values come from the token, not from this table. Starlight's grey scale runs from strongest ink to page background.
65	
66	| Starlight variable | Token | Notes |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `--sl-color-white` | `--bl-ink` | Headings, strongest text |
69	| `--sl-color-gray-1` | `--bl-ink` | |
70	| `--sl-color-gray-2` | `--bl-ink-muted` | Descriptions, card bodies |
71	| `--sl-color-gray-3` | `--bl-ink-subtle` | Eyebrows, captions, meta |
72	| `--sl-color-gray-4` | `--bl-line-strong` | Control borders, hover borders |
73	| `--sl-color-gray-5` | `--bl-line` | |
74	| `--sl-color-gray-6` | `--bl-surface` | Cards, header, AtAGlance |
75	| `--sl-color-gray-7` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | Hovers, code, kbd wells |
76	| `--sl-color-black` | `--bl-bg` | |
77	| `--sl-color-text` | `--bl-ink` | Body copy |
78	| `--sl-color-text-accent` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Links |
79	| `--sl-color-text-invert` | `--bl-on-accent` | Text on the accent |
80	| `--sl-color-accent-low` | `--bl-accent-soft` | Current sidebar item |
81	| `--sl-color-accent` | `--bl-accent` | Primary button, ToC rail |
82	| `--sl-color-accent-high` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Text on `accent-low` |
83	| `--sl-color-bg` | `--bl-bg` | |
84	| `--sl-color-bg-nav` | `--bl-surface` | Solid; the header no longer blurs |
85	| `--sl-color-bg-sidebar` | `--bl-bg` | Separated by a `--bl-line` hairline |
86	| `--sl-color-bg-inline-code` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | |
87	| `--sl-color-bg-accent` | `--bl-accent` | |
88	| `--sl-color-hairline`, `-light`, `-shade` | `--bl-line` | |
89	| `--sl-color-backdrop-overlay` | light `rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.4)`, dark `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` | |
90	| `--sl-color-blue-low` / `blue` / `blue-high` | `surface-sunken` / `ink-muted` / `ink` | Note |
91	| `--sl-color-purple-low` / `purple` / `purple-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Tip |
92	| `--sl-color-green-low` / `green` / `green-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Success badge |
93	| `--sl-color-orange-low` / `orange` / `orange-high` | `caution-soft` / `caution` / `caution` | Caution |
94	| `--sl-color-red-low` / `red` / `red-high` | `danger-soft` / `danger` / `danger` | Danger |
95	| `--sl-shadow-sm` | `--bl-shadow-card` | |
96	| `--sl-shadow-md`, `--sl-shadow-lg` | `--bl-shadow-window` | The search dialog only |
97	
98	Every text pairing here holds at least 4.5:1 in both looks, and every control border and focus ring at least 3:1. Don't introduce a colour that isn't a token.
99	
100	## Type
101	
102	| Where | Style | Size / line height | Weight | Tracking |
103	|---|---|---|---|---|
104	| Splash hero title | `display` | 64 / 64 px (40 / 42 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.035em |
105	| Page title (`h1`) | `heading-1` | 40 / 44 px (32 / 36 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.03em |
106	| `h2` | `heading-2` | 28 / 34 px | 600 | −0.02em |
107	| `h3`, card and pagination titles | `heading-3` | 20 / 28 px | 600 | −0.01em |
108	| `h4` | | 17 / 24 px | 600 | 0 |
109	| Page description, hero tagline | `lede` | 19 / 30 px (17 / 26 below 50rem) | 400 | 0 |
110	| Body | `body` | 16 / 26 px | 400 | 0 |
111	| Sidebar links, tables, asides, AtAGlance | | 15 px, 20–24 px leading | 400 | 0 |
112	| ToC, captions, meta, footer | `small` | 14 / 20 px | 400 | 0 |
113	| Eyebrows: page eyebrow, sidebar group labels, ToC label, table headers, AtAGlance terms | `eyebrow` | 12 / 16 px mono, uppercase | 500 | 0.06em |
114	| Inline code, code blocks | `code` | 14 / 22 px mono | 400 | 0 |
115	
116	So `--sl-text-body: 1rem`, `--sl-line-height: 1.625`, `--sl-text-h1: 2.5rem`, `--sl-text-h2: 1.75rem`, `--sl-text-h3: 1.25rem`, `--sl-text-h4: 1.0625rem`, `--sl-line-height-headings: 1.1`, `--sl-text-code: 0.875rem`. Headings are `--sl-color-white`; there's no bold 700 and no italic heading anywhere.
117	
118	## Corners, borders and depth
119	
120	| Radius | Used on |
121	|---|---|
122	| `--bl-radius-sm` 6 px | `kbd`, inline code, sidebar links, the Steps markers, the feature filter's input |
123	| `--bl-radius-md` 10 px | Buttons, the search field, icon buttons (menu, theme, GitHub), asides, code frames, AtAGlance, Shot |
124	| `--bl-radius-lg` 16 px | Cards, link cards, pagination links, the framed Shot, dialogs, the mobile ToC dropdown |
125	| `--bl-radius-pill` | The header's version badge |
126	
127	Hairlines are `--bl-line`; a hover strengthens a border to `--bl-line-strong`. Nothing lifts, scales or moves on hover.
128	
129	## The parts, in order down the page
130	
131	**Header** (64 px). Solid `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` bottom border, no blur. Gaps of 24 px.
132	
133	- **Lockup** (`SiteTitle.astro`): the blocks mark at 32 px, then **Boppa Llewyn** in Geist 600 17 / 24 px at −0.02em, a `/` in `--bl-ink-subtle` weight 400, the site title (**Frame Job**) in weight 500, and the version badge. Gap 8 px. The badge is mono 500 12 / 16 px, `--bl-ink-subtle`, padding 2 px 8 px, pill-shaped, drawn with an inset 1 px `--bl-line-strong` ring. Below 50rem the company name and the slash hide, leaving the mark, **Frame Job** and the badge. The lockup still links to the docs home.
134	- **Search** (desktop): a 260 × 36 px field on `--bl-surface-sunken` with a `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, the placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle` 14 px, and the ⌘K keys as small `kbd` (20 px tall). Below 50rem it's a 36 px icon button.

139	
140	- Group labels: `eyebrow`, `--bl-ink-subtle`, 8 px above the links, 28 px between groups.
141	- Links: 15 / 20 px, `--bl-ink-muted`, padding 6 px 10 px, `--bl-radius-sm`, 1 px apart. Hover: `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-ink`. Current page: `--bl-accent-soft` background, `--bl-accent-ink` text, weight 550. Keep the existing guard so hover doesn't override the current item.
142	
143	**Page opener** (`PageTitle.astro`, through CSS). The content column is 680 px (`--bl-prose-width`), 56 px from the header.
144	
145	- Eyebrow: `eyebrow` in `--bl-accent-ink`, 12 px above the title. This is the page's one accent-coloured label.
146	- Title: `heading-1`.
147	- Description: `lede` in `--bl-ink-muted`, 16 px below the title.
148	
149	**Body.** Paragraphs and lists 16 px apart; list items 6 px apart. Links are `--bl-accent-ink`, no underline until hover (1 px underline, 3 px offset). `h2` has 48 px above and 12 px below; `h3` 32 px above and 8 px below.
150	
151	**AtAGlance** (`.fj-glance`). `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 32 px above. A two-column grid (terms at their own width, 24 px gap, 10 px between rows). Terms are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`; values 15 / 24 px, menu paths bold, keys as `kbd`, tools as inline code at 13 px.
152	
153	**Shot** (`.fj-shot`). The capture at up to half its pixel width, as now, with a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md` and `--bl-shadow-card`, 32 px above. The caption is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, centred, 10 px below.
154	
155	- **New `frame` prop**: for a full-window capture (a `*.window` screen), `<Shot name="04-editor.window" frame alt="…" />` draws the capture in a window frame instead:
156	  - a 36 px title bar on `--bl-surface` with three 12 px dots in `--bl-line` (not traffic-light colours) and the window title centred in 13 px weight 500 `--bl-ink-subtle`;
157	  - `--bl-radius-lg`, no border, and `--bl-shadow-window`, the site's only large shadow.
158	- Use `frame` on the splash's editor window. Leave partial captures (sheets, inspectors) unframed.
159	
160	**Steps** (Starlight's `<Steps>`). Each number sits in a 28 px square:
161	
162	- `--bl-surface-sunken` fill, 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-sm`;
163	- the number in mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`;
164	- a 1 px `--bl-line` connector down to the next square.
165	
166	Text is indented 48 px, with 20 px between steps.
167	
168	**Tables**. Full width, 15 / 22 px. Headers are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`, 10 px above a `--bl-line-strong` rule. Cells are padded 10 px 12 px 10 px 0, with a `--bl-line` rule under each row. Code in a cell doesn't wrap, as now.
169	
170	**Asides** (`:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution`, `:::danger`). Each is the system's callout:
171	
172	- a full-tint background, the icon, and the type's word as the title;
173	- no border and no left accent bar;
174	- `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 24 px above;
175	- a 20 px icon beside a 15 / 24 px title (weight 600) and a 15 / 24 px body in `--bl-ink-muted`.
176	
177	Show Starlight's aside icon; the current CSS hides it. The colours come from the blue / purple / orange / red mapping above, `-low` for the background and `-high` for the icon and title. The title stays sentence case; drop the mono uppercase it has now.
178	
179	**Code blocks** (Expressive Code). `styleOverrides`:
180	
181	- `borderRadius: '10px'` and `borderColor: 'var(--sl-color-hairline-light)'`;
182	- the code background on `--bl-surface-sunken`;
183	- the frame's title bar on `--bl-surface`, with a `--bl-line` rule under it and its title in mono 500 12 / 16 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, not uppercase.
184	
185	Keep the two syntax themes (`github-light`, `github-dark-default`) and `useStarlightUiThemeColors`. Inline code is mono at 0.875em on `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-radius-sm`, padding 2 px 5 px.
186	
187	**`kbd`**. 24 px tall, 6 px side padding, mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`, on `--bl-surface` with a 1 px `--bl-line` border and a 2 px bottom edge, `--bl-radius-sm`. Use the same anywhere a key is shown, search included.
188	
189	**Buttons** (`LinkButton`). 16 / 24 px weight 550, padding 12 px 20 px, `--bl-radius-md`.
190	
191	- `primary`: `--bl-accent` with `--bl-on-accent` text; hover `--bl-accent-hover`.
192	- `secondary`: `--bl-surface` with `--bl-ink` text and a `--bl-line-strong` border; hover `--bl-surface-sunken`.
193	- `minimal`: `--bl-ink` text, 12 px side padding; hover `--bl-surface-sunken`.
194	
195	**Cards and link cards**. `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-lg`, `--bl-shadow-card`, padding 24 px, 24 px grid gap. The title is `heading-3`; the body is 15 / 22 px `--bl-ink-muted`. Hover strengthens the border to `--bl-line-strong`. A card's icon chip loses its box; the icon is `--bl-ink-subtle`.
196	
197	**Pagination**. Two cards as above, padded 16 px 20 px, 16 px apart, 64 px above. The label (Previous, Next) is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`; the title is `heading-3`.
198	
199	**Footer meta** ("Edit page" and the like). 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, under a `--bl-line` rule 32 px below the pagination. Not mono.
200	
201	**Table of contents** (224 px). Its label is `eyebrow` `--bl-ink-subtle`, 12 px above the list. The list has a 1 px `--bl-line` rail. Links are 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-muted`, padded 5 px 0 5 px 12 px. The current link is `--bl-ink` weight 500, with a 2 px `--bl-accent` rail sitting over the hairline. The mobile ToC bar keeps its current behaviour, recoloured with the same tokens.
202	
203	**Splash** (`template: splash`).
204	
205	- **Hero band**: full viewport width on `--bl-band`, with text in `--bl-on-band`. One way to bleed past the content width is `box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax var(--bl-band); clip-path: inset(0 -100vmax)` on `.hero`.
206	  - Content stays in the 1120 px container (`--bl-content-width`), padded 96 px top and bottom (64 px and 16 px sides below 50rem).
207	  - Two columns, `1fr 192px`, 48 px apart. The Frame Job mark (the existing hero image) shows at 192 px, and above the text at 96 px below 50rem.
208	- **Hero text**: the eyebrow is `eyebrow` in `--bl-on-band` at 80% opacity; the title is `display`; the tagline is `lede` in `--bl-on-band` at 86% opacity, at most 34em wide, 24 px below the title; the actions sit 32 px below it, 12 px apart.
209	- **Below the hero**: 64 px down, the framed editor-window Shot at the full container width. Then the requirements paragraph in `--bl-ink-muted`, 680 px wide, 48 px below. Then "Start here" as an `h2` with a `--bl-line` rule and 64 px above it, and the link cards in two columns (one below 50rem).
210	
211	**Focus**. One rule everywhere: `outline: 2px solid var(--bl-focus); outline-offset: 2px`. It replaces the current two-ring box shadow and holds 3:1 on every surface in both looks.
212	
213	**Motion**. Colour, background and border transitions at 120 ms, nothing else. Keep the reduced-motion rule.
214	
215	**Feature index** (`.fj-filter`, `.fj-features`). The filter box sits on `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` border and `--bl-radius-md`. Its input is on `--bl-bg` with a `--bl-line-strong` border and `--bl-radius-sm`, with a 14 px placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle`. The count is mono 12 px `--bl-ink-subtle`. The table follows "Tables".
216	
217	## Doctored's site
218	
219	`boppa-llewyn.css` is shared rule for rule with Doctored's documentation site (`public-docs/src/styles/custom.css` in the Doctored repository), and its header says to change both together. This handoff covers Frame Job only. Port the finished file to Doctored in a change of its own; until then, the two sites look different. Doctored's lockup reads **Boppa Llewyn / Doctored** with the same mark.
220	
221	## Out of scope
222	
223	- Page content, the sidebar's order and labels, `src/data/features.json`, search behaviour and anything the docs proof reads. The only content edit is the `frame` prop on the splash's Shot.
224	- Shipping the alternate palettes or a palette switcher.
225	- The company website (boppallewyn.com), which has its own handoff.
226	
227	## Checking it
228	
229	- `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` (the last word: links, anchors and imports), `node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs src/content/docs/index.mdx`, and `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py`.
230	- Look at the built site beside `Docs Theme.html`, in both looks, at 1440 px and 390 px. Check the splash, a page with every part (Split clips has steps, a table and AtAGlance), a page with each aside, and the feature index. Nothing should scroll sideways at 390 px.
231	- Search the built CSS for `Cormorant`, `IBM Plex`, `oklch(` and `--bl-brass`. None should remain.

# Handoff: documentation site theme (Boppa Llewyn redesign)

## Overview

This handoff moves the documentation site (`docs/site/`) from the old Boppa Llewyn theme to the new Boppa Llewyn design system. The old theme imitated a furniture workshop: Cormorant Garamond display type, IBM Plex, warm-ebony greys, a cream light look, a brass accent and 2/4/8 px "joinery" corners. The new system is the one the company website and every app's docs share:

- **Type:** Geist for text, Geist Mono for eyebrows, code, keys and versions. No serif anywhere.
- **Colour:** neutral greys, with the logo green as the one accent. The app icons and the company mark supply the rest of the colour.
- **Shape:** 6/10/16 px corners. Hairlines separate things; shadows are limited to a 1 px card shadow and the screenshot window.
- **Brand:** the company mark (three toy blocks) and the name in the header, with the product after it: **Boppa Llewyn / Frame Job**.

Decisions confirmed by the owner:

- The new Boppa Llewyn design system replaces the old theme everywhere.
- The company mark is the building-blocks mark (`assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg`).
- Body type is sans-serif; nothing is set in a serif.

Not yet confirmed: which palette ships. This handoff ships **Neutral Light** for the light look and **Neutral Dark** for the dark look, the pair the design system recommends. The system also has three alternates (Cream & Coral, Field Green, Monochrome). They're in `tokens.css` and switchable in the reference page, so the owner can compare. Changing the palette later means changing two blocks of `tokens.css` and nothing else.

## About the design files

`Docs Theme.html` is a **design reference in HTML**: a static mock of a content page and the splash page, not Starlight's markup. Recreate it in the existing Starlight theme files. Map each part by the tables below, and don't copy the mock's class names. Open it from this folder in a browser (it loads Geist from Google Fonts and the real screens and mark from `docs/site/src/assets/`). The bar at the top switches page, look and palette; `?theme=dark&page=splash&bare=1` does the same from the URL.

## Fidelity

**High fidelity** for colour, type, spacing, corners and borders, in both looks, at 1440 px and 390 px. The page structure doesn't change: the 280 px sidebar and 680 px prose column are the site's current widths, and the table of contents keeps Starlight's own width (224 px in the mock). The header grows from 60 to 64 px (`--sl-nav-height: 4rem`). Icons in the mock are simple stand-ins; keep Starlight's own icons.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `Docs Theme.html` | **The spec.** Content page (Split clips) and splash, light and dark, desktop and phone. |
| `tokens.css` | Every colour, shadow, spacing, radius and font token as `--bl-*` custom properties: Neutral Light under `[data-theme='light']`, Neutral Dark under `[data-theme='dark']`, the three alternate palettes at the end. Generated from the design system; copy it into the site whole rather than retyping values. The type scale is in its closing comment. |
| `assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | The company mark, 1024 × 1024 on the cream app-icon plate. |

## What changes, file by file

All paths are under `docs/site/`.

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/styles/boppa-llewyn.css` | Rewritten on the new tokens: the old `--bl-*` block is replaced by `tokens.css`, the `--sl-*` mapping follows the table below, and every rule below "Site layer" is restyled to the mock. Keep its structure (tokens, mapping, base rules, then the parts Starlight's variables can't reach) and its rule of preferring CSS over overrides. |
| `src/styles/frame-job.css` | `Shot`, `AtAGlance` and the feature index restyled (below). |
| `src/fonts/font-face.css`, `public/fonts/` | Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex removed; Geist and Geist Mono added (below). |
| `astro.config.mjs` | `logo` points at the blocks mark; the two `preload` links name the Geist files; `expressiveCode.styleOverrides` follow "Code blocks". |
| `src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg` | New: copied from this folder. `src/assets/logo.svg` (the Frame Job mark) stays, for the splash hero and anywhere the product is shown. |
| `src/components/SiteTitle.astro` | The lockup (below). |
| `src/components/Shot.astro` | One new optional prop, `frame`, for full-window captures (below). |
| `src/content/docs/index.mdx` | The editor-window `Shot` gains `frame`. No other content changes. |
| `README.md` ("Theme") | Rewritten to describe the new system: the families, the palette pair, the files. |
| `CLAUDE.md` | The `src/fonts/, public/fonts/` row names the new faces, if it names them. |

`ThemeSelect.astro`, `PageTitle.astro` and `Hero.astro` keep their markup; they change through CSS only. `public/favicon.svg` stays the Frame Job icon, because the tab belongs to the product.

## Fonts

- **Geist** (variable, weights 100 to 900) and **Geist Mono** (variable, 100 to 900), both under the SIL Open Font Licence 1.1. Take the `latin` and `latin-ext` WOFF2 subsets from Google Fonts, as the current faces were. Self-host them in `public/fonts/` as now, split by `unicode-range` in `font-face.css`.
- Replace `public/fonts/OFL.txt` with Geist's licence text (it names the Geist Project Authors). Delete every Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex file and rule; nothing uses them afterwards.
- Preload the two `latin` files, Geist and Geist Mono: the page's first screen has both (the header's version badge and the page eyebrow are mono).
- `--sl-font: var(--bl-font-sans)` and `--sl-font-mono: var(--bl-font-mono)`. The stacks in `tokens.css` fall back to the Mac's own San Francisco and SF Mono. Remove `--bl-font-display` and every rule that sets headings in it.

## Starlight's colour variables

Map these in both looks; each value is a token from `tokens.css`, so the light and dark values come from the token, not from this table. Starlight's grey scale runs from strongest ink to page background.

| Starlight variable | Token | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--sl-color-white` | `--bl-ink` | Headings, strongest text |
| `--sl-color-gray-1` | `--bl-ink` | |
| `--sl-color-gray-2` | `--bl-ink-muted` | Descriptions, card bodies |
| `--sl-color-gray-3` | `--bl-ink-subtle` | Eyebrows, captions, meta |
| `--sl-color-gray-4` | `--bl-line-strong` | Control borders, hover borders |
| `--sl-color-gray-5` | `--bl-line` | |
| `--sl-color-gray-6` | `--bl-surface` | Cards, header, AtAGlance |
| `--sl-color-gray-7` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | Hovers, code, kbd wells |
| `--sl-color-black` | `--bl-bg` | |
| `--sl-color-text` | `--bl-ink` | Body copy |
| `--sl-color-text-accent` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Links |
| `--sl-color-text-invert` | `--bl-on-accent` | Text on the accent |
| `--sl-color-accent-low` | `--bl-accent-soft` | Current sidebar item |
| `--sl-color-accent` | `--bl-accent` | Primary button, ToC rail |
| `--sl-color-accent-high` | `--bl-accent-ink` | Text on `accent-low` |
| `--sl-color-bg` | `--bl-bg` | |
| `--sl-color-bg-nav` | `--bl-surface` | Solid; the header no longer blurs |
| `--sl-color-bg-sidebar` | `--bl-bg` | Separated by a `--bl-line` hairline |
| `--sl-color-bg-inline-code` | `--bl-surface-sunken` | |
| `--sl-color-bg-accent` | `--bl-accent` | |
| `--sl-color-hairline`, `-light`, `-shade` | `--bl-line` | |
| `--sl-color-backdrop-overlay` | light `rgba(24, 24, 27, 0.4)`, dark `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.6)` | |
| `--sl-color-blue-low` / `blue` / `blue-high` | `surface-sunken` / `ink-muted` / `ink` | Note |
| `--sl-color-purple-low` / `purple` / `purple-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Tip |
| `--sl-color-green-low` / `green` / `green-high` | `accent-soft` / `accent` / `accent-ink` | Success badge |
| `--sl-color-orange-low` / `orange` / `orange-high` | `caution-soft` / `caution` / `caution` | Caution |
| `--sl-color-red-low` / `red` / `red-high` | `danger-soft` / `danger` / `danger` | Danger |
| `--sl-shadow-sm` | `--bl-shadow-card` | |
| `--sl-shadow-md`, `--sl-shadow-lg` | `--bl-shadow-window` | The search dialog only |

Every text pairing here holds at least 4.5:1 in both looks, and every control border and focus ring at least 3:1. Don't introduce a colour that isn't a token.

## Type

| Where | Style | Size / line height | Weight | Tracking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Splash hero title | `display` | 64 / 64 px (40 / 42 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.035em |
| Page title (`h1`) | `heading-1` | 40 / 44 px (32 / 36 below 50rem) | 600 | −0.03em |
| `h2` | `heading-2` | 28 / 34 px | 600 | −0.02em |
| `h3`, card and pagination titles | `heading-3` | 20 / 28 px | 600 | −0.01em |
| `h4` | | 17 / 24 px | 600 | 0 |
| Page description, hero tagline | `lede` | 19 / 30 px (17 / 26 below 50rem) | 400 | 0 |
| Body | `body` | 16 / 26 px | 400 | 0 |
| Sidebar links, tables, asides, AtAGlance | | 15 px, 20–24 px leading | 400 | 0 |
| ToC, captions, meta, footer | `small` | 14 / 20 px | 400 | 0 |
| Eyebrows: page eyebrow, sidebar group labels, ToC label, table headers, AtAGlance terms | `eyebrow` | 12 / 16 px mono, uppercase | 500 | 0.06em |
| Inline code, code blocks | `code` | 14 / 22 px mono | 400 | 0 |

So `--sl-text-body: 1rem`, `--sl-line-height: 1.625`, `--sl-text-h1: 2.5rem`, `--sl-text-h2: 1.75rem`, `--sl-text-h3: 1.25rem`, `--sl-text-h4: 1.0625rem`, `--sl-line-height-headings: 1.1`, `--sl-text-code: 0.875rem`. Headings are `--sl-color-white`; there's no bold 700 and no italic heading anywhere.

## Corners, borders and depth

| Radius | Used on |
|---|---|
| `--bl-radius-sm` 6 px | `kbd`, inline code, sidebar links, the Steps markers, the feature filter's input |
| `--bl-radius-md` 10 px | Buttons, the search field, icon buttons (menu, theme, GitHub), asides, code frames, AtAGlance, Shot |
| `--bl-radius-lg` 16 px | Cards, link cards, pagination links, the framed Shot, dialogs, the mobile ToC dropdown |
| `--bl-radius-pill` | The header's version badge |

Hairlines are `--bl-line`; a hover strengthens a border to `--bl-line-strong`. Nothing lifts, scales or moves on hover.

## The parts, in order down the page

**Header** (64 px). Solid `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` bottom border, no blur. Gaps of 24 px.

- **Lockup** (`SiteTitle.astro`): the blocks mark at 32 px, then **Boppa Llewyn** in Geist 600 17 / 24 px at −0.02em, a `/` in `--bl-ink-subtle` weight 400, the site title (**Frame Job**) in weight 500, and the version badge. Gap 8 px. The badge is mono 500 12 / 16 px, `--bl-ink-subtle`, padding 2 px 8 px, pill-shaped, drawn with an inset 1 px `--bl-line-strong` ring. Below 50rem the company name and the slash hide, leaving the mark, **Frame Job** and the badge. The lockup still links to the docs home.
- **Search** (desktop): a 260 × 36 px field on `--bl-surface-sunken` with a `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, the placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle` 14 px, and the ⌘K keys as small `kbd` (20 px tall). Below 50rem it's a 36 px icon button.
- **Theme toggle and GitHub link**: 36 px square ghost buttons, `--bl-radius-md`, icon in `--bl-ink-muted`; hover `--bl-surface-sunken` with `--bl-ink`. The toggle keeps its two-state behaviour and its storage key.
- **Menu button** (below 50rem): the same 36 px ghost button, keeping the 44 px hit area the current CSS gives it.

**Sidebar** (280 px). Background `--bl-bg`, a `--bl-line` hairline on the right, padding 32 px 16 px 48 px 24 px.

- Group labels: `eyebrow`, `--bl-ink-subtle`, 8 px above the links, 28 px between groups.
- Links: 15 / 20 px, `--bl-ink-muted`, padding 6 px 10 px, `--bl-radius-sm`, 1 px apart. Hover: `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-ink`. Current page: `--bl-accent-soft` background, `--bl-accent-ink` text, weight 550. Keep the existing guard so hover doesn't override the current item.

**Page opener** (`PageTitle.astro`, through CSS). The content column is 680 px (`--bl-prose-width`), 56 px from the header.

- Eyebrow: `eyebrow` in `--bl-accent-ink`, 12 px above the title. This is the page's one accent-coloured label.
- Title: `heading-1`.
- Description: `lede` in `--bl-ink-muted`, 16 px below the title.

**Body.** Paragraphs and lists 16 px apart; list items 6 px apart. Links are `--bl-accent-ink`, no underline until hover (1 px underline, 3 px offset). `h2` has 48 px above and 12 px below; `h3` 32 px above and 8 px below.

**AtAGlance** (`.fj-glance`). `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 32 px above. A two-column grid (terms at their own width, 24 px gap, 10 px between rows). Terms are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`; values 15 / 24 px, menu paths bold, keys as `kbd`, tools as inline code at 13 px.

**Shot** (`.fj-shot`). The capture at up to half its pixel width, as now, with a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-md` and `--bl-shadow-card`, 32 px above. The caption is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, centred, 10 px below.

- **New `frame` prop**: for a full-window capture (a `*.window` screen), `<Shot name="04-editor.window" frame alt="…" />` draws the capture in a window frame instead:
  - a 36 px title bar on `--bl-surface` with three 12 px dots in `--bl-line` (not traffic-light colours) and the window title centred in 13 px weight 500 `--bl-ink-subtle`;
  - `--bl-radius-lg`, no border, and `--bl-shadow-window`, the site's only large shadow.
- Use `frame` on the splash's editor window. Leave partial captures (sheets, inspectors) unframed.

**Steps** (Starlight's `<Steps>`). Each number sits in a 28 px square:

- `--bl-surface-sunken` fill, 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-sm`;
- the number in mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`;
- a 1 px `--bl-line` connector down to the next square.

Text is indented 48 px, with 20 px between steps.

**Tables**. Full width, 15 / 22 px. Headers are `eyebrow` in `--bl-ink-subtle`, 10 px above a `--bl-line-strong` rule. Cells are padded 10 px 12 px 10 px 0, with a `--bl-line` rule under each row. Code in a cell doesn't wrap, as now.

**Asides** (`:::note`, `:::tip`, `:::caution`, `:::danger`). Each is the system's callout:

- a full-tint background, the icon, and the type's word as the title;
- no border and no left accent bar;
- `--bl-radius-md`, padding 16 px 20 px, 24 px above;
- a 20 px icon beside a 15 / 24 px title (weight 600) and a 15 / 24 px body in `--bl-ink-muted`.

Show Starlight's aside icon; the current CSS hides it. The colours come from the blue / purple / orange / red mapping above, `-low` for the background and `-high` for the icon and title. The title stays sentence case; drop the mono uppercase it has now.

**Code blocks** (Expressive Code). `styleOverrides`:

- `borderRadius: '10px'` and `borderColor: 'var(--sl-color-hairline-light)'`;
- the code background on `--bl-surface-sunken`;
- the frame's title bar on `--bl-surface`, with a `--bl-line` rule under it and its title in mono 500 12 / 16 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, not uppercase.

Keep the two syntax themes (`github-light`, `github-dark-default`) and `useStarlightUiThemeColors`. Inline code is mono at 0.875em on `--bl-surface-sunken`, `--bl-radius-sm`, padding 2 px 5 px.

**`kbd`**. 24 px tall, 6 px side padding, mono 500 13 px `--bl-ink`, on `--bl-surface` with a 1 px `--bl-line` border and a 2 px bottom edge, `--bl-radius-sm`. Use the same anywhere a key is shown, search included.

**Buttons** (`LinkButton`). 16 / 24 px weight 550, padding 12 px 20 px, `--bl-radius-md`.

- `primary`: `--bl-accent` with `--bl-on-accent` text; hover `--bl-accent-hover`.
- `secondary`: `--bl-surface` with `--bl-ink` text and a `--bl-line-strong` border; hover `--bl-surface-sunken`.
- `minimal`: `--bl-ink` text, 12 px side padding; hover `--bl-surface-sunken`.

**Cards and link cards**. `--bl-surface`, a 1 px `--bl-line` border, `--bl-radius-lg`, `--bl-shadow-card`, padding 24 px, 24 px grid gap. The title is `heading-3`; the body is 15 / 22 px `--bl-ink-muted`. Hover strengthens the border to `--bl-line-strong`. A card's icon chip loses its box; the icon is `--bl-ink-subtle`.

**Pagination**. Two cards as above, padded 16 px 20 px, 16 px apart, 64 px above. The label (Previous, Next) is 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`; the title is `heading-3`.

**Footer meta** ("Edit page" and the like). 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-subtle`, under a `--bl-line` rule 32 px below the pagination. Not mono.

**Table of contents** (224 px). Its label is `eyebrow` `--bl-ink-subtle`, 12 px above the list. The list has a 1 px `--bl-line` rail. Links are 14 / 20 px `--bl-ink-muted`, padded 5 px 0 5 px 12 px. The current link is `--bl-ink` weight 500, with a 2 px `--bl-accent` rail sitting over the hairline. The mobile ToC bar keeps its current behaviour, recoloured with the same tokens.

**Splash** (`template: splash`).

- **Hero band**: full viewport width on `--bl-band`, with text in `--bl-on-band`. One way to bleed past the content width is `box-shadow: 0 0 0 100vmax var(--bl-band); clip-path: inset(0 -100vmax)` on `.hero`.
  - Content stays in the 1120 px container (`--bl-content-width`), padded 96 px top and bottom (64 px and 16 px sides below 50rem).
  - Two columns, `1fr 192px`, 48 px apart. The Frame Job mark (the existing hero image) shows at 192 px, and above the text at 96 px below 50rem.
- **Hero text**: the eyebrow is `eyebrow` in `--bl-on-band` at 80% opacity; the title is `display`; the tagline is `lede` in `--bl-on-band` at 86% opacity, at most 34em wide, 24 px below the title; the actions sit 32 px below it, 12 px apart.
- **Below the hero**: 64 px down, the framed editor-window Shot at the full container width. Then the requirements paragraph in `--bl-ink-muted`, 680 px wide, 48 px below. Then "Start here" as an `h2` with a `--bl-line` rule and 64 px above it, and the link cards in two columns (one below 50rem).

**Focus**. One rule everywhere: `outline: 2px solid var(--bl-focus); outline-offset: 2px`. It replaces the current two-ring box shadow and holds 3:1 on every surface in both looks.

**Motion**. Colour, background and border transitions at 120 ms, nothing else. Keep the reduced-motion rule.

**Feature index** (`.fj-filter`, `.fj-features`). The filter box sits on `--bl-surface` with a `--bl-line` border and `--bl-radius-md`. Its input is on `--bl-bg` with a `--bl-line-strong` border and `--bl-radius-sm`, with a 14 px placeholder in `--bl-ink-subtle`. The count is mono 12 px `--bl-ink-subtle`. The table follows "Tables".

## Doctored's site

`boppa-llewyn.css` is shared rule for rule with Doctored's documentation site (`public-docs/src/styles/custom.css` in the Doctored repository), and its header says to change both together. This handoff covers Frame Job only. Port the finished file to Doctored in a change of its own; until then, the two sites look different. Doctored's lockup reads **Boppa Llewyn / Doctored** with the same mark.

## Out of scope

- Page content, the sidebar's order and labels, `src/data/features.json`, search behaviour and anything the docs proof reads. The only content edit is the `frame` prop on the splash's Shot.
- Shipping the alternate palettes or a palette switcher.
- The company website (boppallewyn.com), which has its own handoff.

## Checking it

- `pnpm build` in `docs/site/` (the last word: links, anchors and imports), `node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs src/content/docs/index.mdx`, and `python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py`.
- Look at the built site beside `Docs Theme.html`, in both looks, at 1440 px and 390 px. Check the splash, a page with every part (Split clips has steps, a table and AtAGlance), a page with each aside, and the feature index. Nothing should scroll sideways at 390 px.
- Search the built CSS for `Cormorant`, `IBM Plex`, `oklch(` and `--bl-brass`. None should remain.

content.content:
# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, and `engines` in `package.json` sets the Node it needs. `README.md` has
the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list); SiteTitle, ThemeSelect,
                        PageTitle and Hero are the theme's Starlight overrides
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             boppa-llewyn.css (the theme, shared with Doctored's site) and
                        frame-job.css (this site's components in it); README "Theme"
src/fonts/, public/fonts/  the theme's self-hosted faces and their licence
src/site.ts             the header badge's version, read from the repository's VERSION
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Eyebrow:** the mono label above a page's title is the name of its sidebar group. Set
  `eyebrow:` in the frontmatter only when that name is wrong for the page.
- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out

```
                        PageTitle and Hero are the theme's Starlight overrides

src/fonts/, public/fonts/  the theme's self-hosted faces and their licence
src/site.ts             the header badge's version, read from the repository's VERSION
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

Editing

Split clips

Cut clips in two at the playhead, and see what each piece keeps of the footage, actions, word timings and graphics.

Split cuts a clip in two at the playhead, so you can trim, move or remove one piece without touching the other. There's no separate blade or razor tool. Split does that job.

Menu
Clip ▸ Split
Keys
⌘T
Where
The scissors button in the timeline bar
Tools
split

Split at the playhead

  1. Move the playhead to the frame you want to cut on.
  2. Select the clips to cut, or select nothing to cut everything under the playhead.
  3. Press ⌘T, choose Clip ▸ Split, or click the scissors button in the timeline bar.
What's selectedWhat gets cut
One or more clipsEach selected clip the playhead is inside
NothingEvery clip under the playhead on every unlocked track

It's one undo step, named Split, however many clips it cuts. If nothing can be cut, Frame Job beeps and nothing changes.

Asides

The four Starlight asides, as the system's callout: a full tint, an icon and the word. No left bar.

Note
The cut lands on the project's frame grid.
Tip
Select nothing to cut every clip under the playhead at once.
Caution
Sound fades are copied to both pieces, so set them again where you don't want them.
Danger
Reserved for what loses work. The docs have none today.

With an agent

split cuts at a time you give it, or at the playhead if you leave the time out. See Tools: cutting and deleting.

# Connect Claude Code to Frame Job
claude mcp add framejob -- "/Applications/Frame Job.app/Contents/Helpers/framejob-mcp"

    Add the docs theme handoff for the Boppa Llewyn redesign
    
    designs/design_handoff_docs_theme/ hands the documentation site's move
    from the old workshop theme (Cormorant Garamond, IBM Plex, brass, warm
    greys) to the new Boppa Llewyn design system: Geist and Geist Mono,
    Neutral Light and Neutral Dark, the logo green as the one accent, 6/10/16
    corners and the building-blocks company mark in the header.
    
    - Docs Theme.html: the reference, a content page and the splash in both
      looks at desktop and phone width, using the site's real screens.
    - tokens.css: generated from the design system's tokens.json.
    - README.md: the Starlight variable mapping, the type scale, each part's
      metrics, the file-by-file change, fonts, Doctored parity and checks.
    
    Docs only; no site file changes. Verified: name_residue.py and
    docs_site_proof.py pass; the reference renders without overflow at
commit d40d1f81cfeb30d427461263652d96ba246b89be
Author: Kevin Galligan <kgalligan@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Nov 6 20:03:20 2026 -0500

    The documentation site wears Boppa Llewyn, the theme of Doctored's documentation site
    
    boppa-llewyn.css is Doctored's public-docs custom.css rule for rule (only
    Prettier's formatting differs), with its self-hosted fonts (Cormorant
    Garamond, IBM Plex Sans and Mono, OFL) and its four Starlight overrides:
    SiteTitle (the mark, the wordmark and a version badge read from VERSION),
    ThemeSelect (a two-state toggle), PageTitle and Hero (a mono eyebrow, the
    sidebar group's name unless a page's `eyebrow:` frontmatter says otherwise).
    frame-job.css now holds only the site's own components (Shot, AtAGlance, the
    feature index) drawn with the theme's tokens; the fontsource packages are
    gone. README "Theme" and docs/site/CLAUDE.md say where each part lives and
    that the theme changes in both sites together.
    
    Verified: pnpm build (366 pages, every internal link valid), pnpm
    format:check, check-pages.mjs and docs_site_proof.py with 0 problems,
    headless screenshots of both sites side by side (home in both looks, a
    feature page, /features/, a phone width), and make gate PASS (784 s).
    
    Owed: nothing for the theme. The site's public URL, and with it astro's
    `site`, the README's links and Help ▸ Frame Job Help, waits on the owner's
    Netlify step.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Entire-Checkpoint: 01M6SRG340DBSYC4GDQ690JXK1

I've written the spec to /Users/kevingalligan/.claude/litecode/framejob/docs-theme-redesign/01-spec.md (75 lines, no STOP). It follows spec-template.md, and I explored only the worktree /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob-ai-docs-int, read-only.

**What it covers:** Every item in the handoff README's "What changes, file by file", restyling only `docs/site/`. The README's sections stay the rule-by-rule spec. `Docs Theme.html` is the picture to match.

**Decisions I took where the README leaves a choice:**
1. **Tokens file:** `tokens.css` becomes its own file, `docs/site/src/styles/tokens.css`. It is copied whole, alternate palettes included, then Prettier-formatted with no value changed. It loads after `font-face.css` and before `boppa-llewyn.css`, and `customCss` gets that order.
2. **Shot's `frame` prop:** it is `frame?: boolean`. The window title comes from `Astro.locals.starlightRoute.siteTitle`, the title bar is `aria-hidden`, and a framed Shot drops the half-width cap so it fills the splash's 1120 px container.
3. **Logo:** the config is `{ src: './src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg', alt: 'Boppa Llewyn' }`. `SiteTitle` draws the mark at 32 px with `alt=""` because the name follows as text. The lockup markup is: `.company`, then `.sep`, then `.wordmark`, then `.version`.
4. **ThemeSelect, PageTitle and Hero:** markup and scripts stay unchanged. Their `<style>` blocks and header comments may change so that no old token or old size is left in them. The README lists none of these three files, but `ThemeSelect` still uses `--bl-radius-1`.
5. **Code-block overrides:** Starlight's own Expressive Code settings win over the config's `styleOverrides` (`@expressive-code/core` index.js lines 3028–3029). So the code background, the active-tab background and the title type go in `boppa-llewyn.css`. Only the keys Starlight doesn't set go in the config.
6. **Splash:** every `h2` on the splash gets the hairline rule with 64 px above, as the mock's `.splash h2` does. The phone hero is left-aligned, as in the mock. The search field sits at the right of its header column.
7. **Fonts:** four files, `Geist-Variable-latin(-ext).woff2` and `GeistMono-Variable-latin(-ext).woff2`, weights 100–900. Geist has no italic face.
8. **Smaller choices:** transitions use a literal `120ms` because the new tokens have no duration. The feature count is mono but not uppercase.

**Verification in the spec:**
- `pnpm build`, which should give 366 pages.
- `pnpm format:check` and `check-pages.mjs`.
- `docs_site_proof.py` and `name_residue.py`, which is cheap and reads the new text files.
- A grep of the built CSS for `Cormorant`, `IBM Plex`, `oklch(` and `--bl-brass`.
- A grep of the sources for any old token left behind.
- `ls dist/fonts`.
- `shot.sh` captures in both looks at 1440 and 500 px of six pages, each compared with the mock. The pages are `/`, `/editing/splitting/`, `/color/animate-a-grade/`, `/audio/synchronize-audio/`, `/recording/cursor-files/` and `/features/`.

**Decisions I took where the README leaves a choice:**
1. **Tokens file:** `tokens.css` becomes its own file, `docs/site/src/styles/tokens.css`. It is copied whole, alternate palettes included, then Prettier-formatted with no value changed. It loads after `font-face.css` and before `boppa-llewyn.css`, and `customCss` gets that order.
2. **Shot's `frame` prop:** it is `frame?: boolean`. The window title comes from `Astro.locals.starlightRoute.siteTitle`, the title bar is `aria-hidden`, and a framed Shot drops the half-width cap so it fills the splash's 1120 px container.
3. **Logo:** the config is `{ src: './src/assets/boppa-llewyn-blocks.svg', alt: 'Boppa Llewyn' }`. `SiteTitle` draws the mark at 32 px with `alt=""` because the name follows as text. The lockup markup is: `.company`, then `.sep`, then `.wordmark`, then `.version`.
4. **ThemeSelect, PageTitle and Hero:** markup and scripts stay unchanged. Their `<style>` blocks and header comments may change so that no old token or old size is left in them. The README lists none of these three files, but `ThemeSelect` still uses `--bl-radius-1`.
5. **Code-block overrides:** Starlight's own Expressive Code settings win over the config's `styleOverrides` (`@expressive-code/core` index.js lines 3028–3029). So the code background, the active-tab background and the title type go in `boppa-llewyn.css`. Only the keys Starlight doesn't set go in the config.
6. **Splash:** every `h2` on the splash gets the hairline rule with 64 px above, as the mock's `.splash h2` does. The phone hero is left-aligned, as in the mock. The search field sits at the right of its header column.
7. **Fonts:** four files, `Geist-Variable-latin(-ext).woff2` and `GeistMono-Variable-latin(-ext).woff2`, weights 100–900. Geist has no italic face.
8. **Smaller choices:** transitions use a literal `120ms` because the new tokens have no duration. The feature count is mono but not uppercase.
